numeral.purpose: The one giant engraved money figure per sheet; Rp prefix set at headline size.

headline.purpose: Page, section and dialog titles, note name plates.

body.purpose: Everything read or tapped; list amounts.

label.purpose: Field labels, meta lines, tab labels; the 12px floor.

stamp.purpose: Uppercase only inside rubber stamps and the Catat seal.

serial.purpose: FNC·DDMMYY·NNNN on every note and stub.

shadows.name: seal-paper-ring
shadows.purpose: Cuts the Catat seal out of the bar or note it overlaps. The only shadow in the system.

shadows.name: field-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus on text fields, with the border going full ink.

motion.name: ease-press
motion.purpose: Every print motion: stub slide-in, rosette turn, stamp thump.

motion.name: stub-in
motion.purpose: A new stub joins today's stack.

motion.name: numeral-roll
motion.purpose: The jatah numeral rolls to its new value after a log.

motion.name: rosette-turn
motion.purpose: The note's rosette turns a few degrees per log.

motion.name: stamp-thump
motion.purpose: LUNAS lands the moment something is paid.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All of the above collapse to an instant change under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar replaces the bottom bar; the seal moves onto the note's edge.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Three-column dashboard: note spans two, stubs in the right column.

narrative.overview:
Money you can hold. Every surface is printed from one press: navy intaglio ink on cream note paper, hairline rules, corner registration marks, procedural guilloche rosettes and serial numbers. Today's allowance is a single banknote-like sheet with one giant engraved numeral, not a grid of equal-weight KPI cards. Wallets, envelopes and goals are notes in their own denomination color; transactions are serial-numbered stubs torn off the note; status is a rubber stamp and the color of the note's security thread.

Density is calm and ledger-like. Three text sizes and one numeral face carry the whole hierarchy, so a figure's importance is told by size and face, never by a colored tile or chip. State is told by form as well as hue (doubled, dashed, filled, struck) so nothing relies on color alone. Dark mode is the same note printed in reverse: cream ink on navy stock, still matte.

The world is banknote grammar, never banknote reproduction: no Garuda, Bank Indonesia marks, portraits or real Rupiah artwork. Rejected outright: the fintech dashboard of equal cards, chips and charts; gradients, glass, glow and drop shadows; nested cards.
keyCharacteristics: One printed sheet per idea, flat paper with a 1px ink hairline and four registration corners.
Bricolage Grotesque heavy figures for money and headings (1, 4 and 7 unmistakable at every size); Archivo for everything you read or tap.
Green, ochre and red mean money status and nothing else.
Every money figure states its scope in words next to it (hari ini, bulan ini, dari tagihan, dari profil).
Guilloche rosettes and the wavy microtext rule are the only ornament.
Logging re-prints the note: the numeral rolls, the rosette turns, a stub slides into the stack.

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, ochre and red are reserved for Aman, Mepet and Habis. A wallet, envelope, goal, category or decoration never prints in them; it takes a denomination (blue, violet, teal, slate).

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Outside status and denominations, everything is ink or soft ink on paper. No Tailwind default palette, no tinted icon tiles.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: Meta 12, body 15, head 22, plus the clamp numeral. Nothing else in the app, and nothing below 12px.

rules.name: The Money Column Rule
rules.body: Every rupiah figure is set with tabular lining numerals so amounts align in columns, and dates are glued with no-break spaces so "Kam, 8 Okt" never splits.

rules.name: The Scope Rule
rules.body: Every money figure states its scope in words beside it: "Sisa jatah hari ini", "Sisa bulan ini", "Terpakai hari ini", "(dari tagihan)". A bare total is not allowed.

rules.name: The Named Figure Rule
rules.body: An uppercase, tracked 12px line is permitted only as the heading that names the figure directly below it (SISA JATAH HARI INI) or as a navigation group name. It is never a decorative kicker introducing another heading.

rules.name: The Thumb Seal Rule
rules.body: On phones (<768px) the Catat seal lives in the center of the bottom bar on every page. On md+ it overlaps the jatah note's lower edge. One seal per screen, never two microphones.

rules.name: The Printed Depth Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, gradients, glass, blur or glow. If something must sit above something else, give it a hairline or a paper ring.

dos: Do print wallets, envelopes, slips and goals in blue, violet, teal or slate, with paper-colored type.
Do state the scope of every money figure in words next to it (hari ini, bulan ini, dari tagihan, dari profil).
Do use exactly three text sizes (meta 12, body 15, head 22) plus the clamp numeral, with 12px as the floor.
Do show state by form as well as hue, and repeat it in words: doubled = mepet or melewati jatah, dashed record edge = belum sinkron, struck = dihapus, solid fill = habis or LUNAS.
Do keep every touch target at least 44px and the Catat seal at least 72px.
Do put a serial (FNC·DDMMYY·NNNN) on every note and stub.
Do honor reduced motion: the numeral swaps instantly, stubs and stamps appear without movement.
donts: Don't use green, ochre or red for anything but Aman, Mepet and Habis.
Don't use the rubber-stamp form for anything but Aman, Mepet, Habis, Tertunda sinkron and LUNAS; every other state is a plain StateLabel.
Don't strike through anything that is not dihapus.
Don't put a dashed edge on a record unless it is belum sinkron.
Don't use gradients, glass or backdrop blur, glow, or drop shadows.
Don't nest a bordered card inside a card; one sheet per idea, divided by hairlines.
Don't put a small uppercase kicker above a heading.
Don't set any text below 12px or outside the three sizes and the numeral.
Don't show a money figure without its scope.
Don't reproduce real Rupiah artwork (Garuda, Bank Indonesia marks, portraits).
